result:
`benchmark.json` is written and validates as JSON — 8 tasks, all fixtures inline.

The environment is a documented house CLI for embedded terminal panes (`panectl`: send / capture / blocking await with a required timeout capped at 600s / a deprecated poll command), which gives the sandbox a concrete, offline-runnable surface without fingerprinting any implementation. Tasks are graded on artifacts an agent can produce with file tools alone.

| id | kind | what it probes |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | ordinary | Dispatch a 8–15 min suite into a named pane and return a result: one bounded blocking wait, scoped past the echo, artifact check, honest timeout |
| T2 | hard | 40–70 min job vs. a 600s per-call ceiling — resume correctly rescoped; existing script polls, matches the whole buffer, and exits 0 on giving up |
| T3 | edge | Stale marker: pane buffer already holds `BUNDLE OK (3.3.9)`; also must split timeout from build failure and propagate to the caller |
| T4 | variation | Three panes (must pick `worker`), user offers to watch and asks for "no ceremony" — the wait must survive both pressures |
| T5 | activation-negative | Plain synchronous shell work with the pane docs sitting in the repo; success is restraint plus correct exit aggregation |
| T6 | hard | Postmortem of a transcript with five distinct failures (unwatched turn, poll rounds, stale marker, no bound, no artifact check) → rules in AGENTS.md |
| T7 | edge | An expired wait whose tail contains a bait line `export complete for shard b of 4`; must not flip status to `complete` |
| T8 | activation-negative | One-way relay with no read path — dispatch honestly, invent no wait, don't sleep-and-claim |

Packets state invariants and disqualifiers rather than a model answer, and note explicitly where multiple shapes (loop structure, return type, status wording) are all acceptable.
